guardrails.title: Requirement Verification Criteria
guardrails.body: At the Spec stage, each requirement shall state what will be checked, how it will be checked, and the observable expected result that determines whether the requirement is satisfied. For testable behavior, define the relevant input or conditions and expected outcome; for requirements not verifiable by automated tests, define a concrete inspection method and acceptance condition. Rewrite vague goals, unsupported future guarantees, and unspecified verification methods into checkable conditions. Evaluate the specification's verification plan and acceptance conditions, not whether implementation or test execution has already occurred. Implementation diffs, test code, and test execution results belong to later stages; their absence at the Spec stage is not a violation of this rule.

guardrails.title: Validate User Input at Entry Point
guardrails.body: When adding or modifying CLI commands, the spec shall list each user-facing argument and its validation requirements (type, format, range). Arguments used only by internal automation shall be marked as internal. The implementation shall validate user-facing arguments at the entry point before passing them to internal functions.

findings.observed: R5 names multiple positional arguments and option values, then says their values, empty-value rules, and conditional combinations follow existing handlers or domain validators. It does not list the applicable type, format, and range requirements for those arguments.
The proposed valid/invalid boundary checks do not identify the relevant inputs and expected outcomes for the arguments whose rules are deferred to existing validators.

The inventory lists arguments and option kinds, but delegates value type, format, empty-value rules, and limits to handlers and later requirements. It does not state those validation requirements for each user-facing argument.
R6 gives concrete limits for some tokens, but assigns other IDs, paths, and resource inputs to individual owners or to unspecified existing limits. Their validation requirements are not listed.
For the inputs governed by unspecified owner-specific or existing limits, the planned boundary tests do not state the input conditions and observable acceptance or rejection results.
